instagram.author: synsation_
instagram.body:
@github what’s going on 😭
What the heck is going on with GitHub? Because over the last 90 days, reliability has tanked. 84% uptime and 94 incidents. April was the worst at 78%. And if you zoom out, it's 256 incidents in just one year. 48 incidents that are major. You see, this is a system that developers rely on. We used to not second guess, if you merge a pull request, it's done. But now Actions is breaking and in April the merge queue was actually producing bad commits, silently reverting code from previously merged PRs. Mitchell Hashimoto, the guy behind Terraform and Vagrant, kept a journal where every day when GitHub wasn't working for him, he put an X. And after 18 years of him using GitHub, he is done and he is taking Ghosty and leaving the platform. GitHub did come forward after April's outages and explained that agentic development and AI tools have caused a massive spike in commits, PRs, and repos, and they're struggling to keep up. Here's the thing is that GitHub built a near monopoly of where code lives, and now we're seeing what happens when a single point of failure actually fails. 99.9% availability is the industry baseline and typically higher, and GitHub is well below that right now. When prominent figures like Hashimoto say, "I'm done", how many people actually follow? And do they move to GitLab or any of the other alternatives that exist, or is there something new that's going to come forward that is better built for the agentic era and how things are changing with the current software development environment?

instagram.author: parth.builds
instagram.body:
You think you’ve used GitHub a lot… but have you really used it?
Comment “Repo” for the repository link.

Most people just browse projects for 5–10 minutes and move on.
“You notice a bug, UI issue, or a missing feature… and just scroll away.”

That’s exactly where GitHub Issues comes in.

Instead of ignoring it → drop an issue.
That’s how real open source starts.
And if you go one step further → you can fix it with a pull request.

Small observation → real impact → actual contribution.

tiktok.author: devbysami
tiktok.body:
GitHub is Dying. | #software#programming#ai
Github is dying. I know this sounds crazy, but hear me out. For the last couple of weeks they have been having these crazy outages. So much so that Mitchell Hashimoto, the creator of The Ghostly Terminal, has decided to move off of Github after 18 years. And it's not just him. Even people like me are considering moving their projects off of Github just because of their huge reliability issues. And although that is one of the main reasons, it's not the only reason why. It's also insane things happening. Gitlab randomly deciding to revert changes that you already merged on a PR. Now this doesn't sound like such a big deal for the average person, but for you as a developer, I don't think you can understand how fucking crazy that is. Imagine working on a feature for 5 days. You spend these huge resources to just get this feature done, and finally you have it. You merge the PR, your entire team is happy, you get a bonus or whatever, and then it's just all fucking gone. Gitlab randomly decided to show you their middle finger and just remove it all. Now that in itself is completely unacceptable. However, this can still be excused because you are Gitlab. But what cannot be excused is the fact that you are hacked by a singular samicolon. It just fucking can't. On April 28th stagnits from with security posted this on Twitter we achieved RTU of Git Hub and got Access to millions of repositories belonging to other users and organizations. All it took was a single Git push. Are you fucking kidding me? The company that we are supposed to trust with all our data, code and all these secrets just gets hacked by a semicolon? And that's just a vulnerability. The actual exploit is a single git push. Is this reality? And if you don't understand the extent of severity for remote code execution, you basically can fuck up the entire company. And we are so, so lucky this was a white hat hacker. If this was black hat, everything would be cooked. When I Learned of this, this was my response. Long story short, Github is just not as reliable as it once was, with a near 85% uptime. And if you know anything about software, that uptime is horrendous. Even SHE or AI which is like the company that I lead has a uptime of 99.9% and that is actually the standard, believe it or not. 85% is not fucking normal. It just doesn't happen in the world of software. Except for like anthropic and get up. For some reason they just fucking vibe code everything, including their infrastructure. I don't understand how you manage to fuck up this bad. Like even if I use clots on it for it wouldn't be this bad. I urge you to reconsider whether you want to continue using Git Hub or move to something like Gitlab. And obviously this...
